feature: The type and shape settings reach everything you picked
summary: Pick several labels and the Text settings stay in the panel and speak for all of them: one size, font or weight reaches every one in a single undo step. Same for shapes: pick two boxes and Thickness and Corner Radius reach both. Where the picked layers disagree the setting reads Mixed, and setting it makes them agree.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. No flags to turn on.

try.do: Type three text labels on a blank canvas, then press Escape.
Band-select all three with the Select tool.
Set one of them to a different size first, reselect all three, and read the Size menu: it says Mixed.
Pick 14 pt from the Size menu once, and watch all three change.
Press Command Z once: all three go back at the same time.
Draw two rectangles, make one thicker on its own, then band-select both.
Pull Corner Radius once and watch both round; Command Z once puts both back.
Shift-click a label together with a rectangle: both sections are there, each saying it applies to 1 of the 2.

evaluate: With three labels picked, does the Text section read as speaking for all three, or does it look like it is describing one of them?
Is Mixed in a menu with no label beside it clear enough, or do the Font, Size and Weight menus need their names on screen?
Picking an arrow and a rectangle together leaves only Thickness. Is losing the corner and arrowhead rows the right call, or would you rather see them dimmed so you can tell they exist?
The Caption field disappears the moment you pick a second arrow, because one field cannot give three arrows different words. Does that feel right, or should it stay and edit the first one?
When a label and a box are picked together, two sections each say they apply to 1 of the 2. Is that helpful, or is it too much small print?
rough: The three type menus have no labels on screen, so a Size menu reading Mixed is a bare word in a row of three. Hover text now says which is which, but the row could be clearer. Filed as a follow-up.
A rectangle still shows two different sliders both called Corner Radius, one in its own section and one under Effects. Already filed as one-corner-radius-not-two.

Making a label bold used to wrap its words onto a second line, because a restyle always re-measured inside the box's old width. A box still hugging its words now re-hugs them at the new type. A box someone stretched keeps the width it was given, as before. Current is untouched: it has no stretching.
A label whose box was stretched DOWNWARD still loses that extra height when its type changes. Pre-existing, not touched here.
Screen Recording was granted, so every picture in this audit is a real window capture, not an offscreen render.
